high.title: Good News for Banks: State Bank of Vietnam Officially Loosens LDR Ratio, Vietcombank, BIDV and VietinBank Can Lend Additional Tens of Thousands of Billions VND
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam issued Circular 08/2026/TT-NHNN amending regulations on safety ratios for banks, notably changing how State Treasury deposits are calculated in the loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR). Previously, 100% of term deposits from State Treasury were excluded from LDR calculations. Now, only 80% will be excluded, meaning 20% of State Treasury term deposits can be included in the denominator. This change is significant for state-owned commercial banks holding large State Treasury deposits, potentially freeing up tens of thousands of billions VND for lending. The relaxation reduces pressure on banks to mobilize retail and corporate deposits to meet safety ratios, and may cool deposit rate competition as banks no longer need to aggressively raise input rates to balance credit growth. This policy change takes effect immediately from May 15, 2026, providing substantial lending headroom for major banks.

high.title: One Bank Approved by SBV to Increase Charter Capital by Over 6,000 Billion VND
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam approved SeABank's capital increase of up to 6.238 trillion VND through two methods: issuing shares for 2025 dividend payment (maximum 5.838 trillion VND) and employee stock ownership program (maximum 400 billion VND). This will boost SeABank's charter capital to 34.688 trillion VND. The capital increase aims to enhance competitive capacity and ensure capital adequacy ratios (CAR) meet Basel III international standards, creating a solid foundation for credit activities, technology investment and comprehensive operations. This represents significant strengthening of SeABank's capital base to support future growth and regulatory compliance in Vietnam's evolving banking landscape.

high.title: Banks May Soon Have Additional Tens of Thousands of Billions VND to Lend?
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam is seeking feedback on draft amendments to Circular 22/2019 regarding safety ratios for banks. The key change involves excluding only 80% of State Treasury term deposits from the LDR calculation denominator, meaning 20% will now count toward mobilized funds. This significant change benefits state-owned banks with large State Treasury deposit volumes, potentially reducing pressure to mobilize retail and corporate deposits to meet safety ratios. Deposit rates could cool further as banks no longer need to compete aggressively on input rates to balance credit growth. Expert Nguyen Danh Thai notes this could provide substantial additional lending capacity for the banking system, particularly benefiting large state-owned banks and supporting monetary policy transmission through the financial system.

high.title: Bad Debt at Many Banks Increases Sharply: Two Banks Have Bad Debt Balance Exceeding 40,000 Billion VND
high.summary: Bad debt across 27 listed banks reached 292.16 trillion VND by March 31, 2026, increasing 28.065 trillion VND (+11%) compared to end-2025. Most banks recorded rising trends, with only VietinBank, NamABank and ABBank showing decreases. BIDV leads with 42.655 trillion VND in bad debt (+7.678 trillion VND, +22% in Q1), followed by Sacombank at 41.498 trillion VND (+1.361 trillion VND, +3%). VPBank ranks third with 37.284 trillion VND (+5.819 trillion VND, +18%). The sharp increase in bad debt across the banking system raises concerns about asset quality deterioration and potential impacts on bank profitability and lending capacity. This trend requires close monitoring as it could affect monetary policy transmission and overall financial stability if it continues escalating.

medium.title: Which Bank Offers Highest Interest Rates for Deposits Currently?
medium.summary: Several banks including HDBank, NCB, and Vikki Bank are offering promotional rates of 8-9%/year for 6+ month terms with minimum deposits. OCB offers 8.5%/year for 6-12 month terms but requires minimum 1,000 billion VND deposit. Cake by VPBank adds up to 1.5%/year bonus for first-time depositors, potentially reaching 8.9%/year. Many banks are adjusting rates upward to attract deposits.

medium.title: Agribank No Longer the Bank with Most Deposits, How is Banking Industry Order Changing?
medium.summary: BIDV has overtaken Agribank as the largest deposit mobilizer, reaching over 1.95 trillion VND in 2024 versus Agribank's 1.91 trillion VND. This historic shift reflects changing dynamics from digitalization and urbanization trends, ending Agribank's decades-long dominance in deposit mobilization despite its extensive branch network.

medium.title: 8 Banks Pump Additional 66,000 Billion VND into Real Estate Business: Nearly Half from Largest Private Bank
medium.summary: VPBank leads with 31.046 trillion VND increase in real estate lending (+15%) reaching 238.473 trillion VND, making it the largest real estate lender among reporting banks. MB followed with 10.707 trillion VND increase. The continued flow of credit into real estate reflects banks' confidence in the sector's recovery prospects.

medium.title: Expert: VN-Index Soon to Reach 2,000 Points
medium.summary: VN-Index established new historical high at 1,925 points, surpassing previous record of 1,918 points. Money flow is rotating from Vingroup stocks to banking and oil & gas sectors. Experts see potential for continued upward momentum toward 2,000 points, though liquidity remains moderate and foreign investors continue net selling.

medium.title: Dragon Capital Expert Identifies Three Catalysts That Could Open New Cycle for Vietnamese Securities
medium.summary: Dragon Capital identifies three structural drivers for Vietnamese stock market: market upgrade (FTSE emerging market classification and potential MSCI inclusion in 2-3 years), demographic dividend, and infrastructure development. MSCI inclusion could trigger significant passive fund inflows, transforming market dynamics and providing sustainable growth catalyst.
